subject: regw
note: Open questions of the Regulation W affiliate definition (12 CFR 223.2 and the control definitions of 223.3), row affiliates-2026-11, recorded 2026-11-28 from NOTES.md (‘Forks and open questions’, ‘Open questions for a lawyer’) and independent-readings.md. Ten entries, all open: no domain expert has read this encoding against Part 223, so none is a legal ruling. Where NOTES.md states a default as the encoder's own, taken.rationale carries the label ‘decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review’, the date being that of the commit that wrote the NOTES.md paragraph. F3 to F6 are switches: enumerated inputs the caller supplies in the record `Readings` (regw-nouns.l4), both constructors execute, and the tests assert both. The code writes no default; the default each entry names is the first constructor of the declaration and the value the tests call `default readings`. They are recorded as delegated-to-fact with the field named, because the register's interpretation-field arm requires a TYPICALLY default and these modules have none. Reading ids are camel-case names; the exact constructor name is given in the description. Witness line numbers are lines of the .l4 files at the commit that deposited this register. Questions about transactions, limits, collateral and exemptions are in the register of transactions-2026-11, which holds byte copies of these modules and does not repeat these entries. Other assumptions stated in NOTES.md (for example 223.3(g)(3) applied to an individual controller) are not in this register.

source.quote: A company controls securities, assets, or other ownership interests owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by any subsidiary (including a subsidiary depository institution) of the company.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(1)(i): “owns, controls, or has power to vote 25 percent or more of any class of voting securities of the other company”
12 CFR 223.3(ii): “a company that is controlled by the specified company”

readings.description: Control is the least fixed point of its own definition: start from no control and add a pair only once the text makes it true given the pairs already added. Take A holding 15 percent of B and of C, with B and C each holding 15 percent of the other: A controls neither, holds 15 percent of each, and the 25 percent test is not met.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(ii): “a company that is controlled by the specified company”

readings.description: A controls B and C. Then it controls their holdings and holds 15 + 15 = 30 percent of each, and the test is met. The text is consistent with this state as well, so the definition has two fixed points.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(1)(i): “owns, controls, or has power to vote 25 percent or more of any class of voting securities of the other company”

taken.rationale: The module computes the least fixed point: a group of companies that each hold less than 25 percent of one another is not found to control one another merely because they could be read as doing so (regw-control.l4, header comment, lines 8-11). The text does not say which fixed point is meant; NOTES.md calls it a question for a lawyer.

witnesses: regw-control-tests.l4 lines 145-159, section ‘Cross-holdings: two fixed points’: the control step leaves {A controls B, A controls C} unchanged, and the relation computed is the empty set
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘Cross-holdings: control has two fixed points (open question)’, and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 1.
Same question for the affiliate definition: F2. Only the least fixed point is computed; the other state is asserted as a state the step leaves unchanged, not as a result.

source.quote: Any company that is a subsidiary of the member bank, unless the company is: (i) A depository institution; (ii) A financial subsidiary; (iii) Directly controlled by: (A) One or more affiliates (other than depository institution affiliates) of the member bank;

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(2): “Any company, including any subsidiary of the member bank, that is controlled by a company that controls the member bank”
12 CFR 223.3(ii): “a company that is controlled by the specified company”

readings.description: The set of affiliates is the least set the text supports. P holds 100 percent of Bank; Bank holds 30 percent of S1 and of S2; S1 and S2 each hold 25 percent of the other. With only P found, neither S1 nor S2 is an affiliate: each is a subsidiary of Bank that no affiliate directly controls.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(b)(1)(iii)(A): “Directly controlled by: (A) One or more affiliates (other than depository institution affiliates) of the member bank”
12 CFR 223.2(a)(2): “Any company, including any subsidiary of the member bank, that is controlled by a company that controls the member bank”

readings.description: With P, S1 and S2 all found, each of S1 and S2 is an affiliate through (a)(2) and is directly controlled by the other, which is an affiliate, so the exclusion in (b)(1) does not apply and the set holds. A cross-holding between two bank subsidiaries would then lift the exclusion from both.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(b)(1)(iii)(A): “Directly controlled by: (A) One or more affiliates (other than depository institution affiliates) of the member bank”
12 CFR 223.2(a)(2): “Any company, including any subsidiary of the member bank, that is controlled by a company that controls the member bank”

taken.rationale: The module takes the least fixed point, as it does for control (regw-affiliate.l4, header comment, lines 8-11). NOTES.md notes that under the other reading a cross-holding between two bank subsidiaries would lift the exclusion from both.

witnesses: regw-affiliate-tests.l4 lines 306-317, section ‘Two fixed points of the affiliate definition’: with only P found neither S1 nor S2 is an affiliate; with P, S1 and S2 found each is; the affiliates computed number one
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘The affiliate definition has two fixed points as well (open question; the least is taken)’, and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 7.
Companion of F1: the same self-reference, at a different site, in the affiliate definition rather than the control definition.

source.quote: Any company, including any subsidiary of the member bank, that is controlled by a company that controls the member bank

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(f): “includes a member bank and a depository institution”

readings.description: Constructor `The member bank is not its own affiliate`. The member bank is left out of the set of its own affiliates.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(2): “Any company, including any subsidiary of the member bank, that is controlled by a company that controls the member bank”
12 CFR 223.3(f): “includes a member bank and a depository institution”

readings.description: Constructor `The member bank is its own affiliate on the literal words`. A member bank that has a parent is a company controlled by a company that controls it, and 223.2(b) does not exclude it, so on the literal words it is its own affiliate.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(2): “Any company, including any subsidiary of the member bank, that is controlled by a company that controls the member bank”
12 CFR 223.3(f): “includes a member bank and a depository institution”

taken.rationale: decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review: the section's purpose is the bank's dealings with others. Under the literal reading the member bank should be flagged as a depository institution, or (b)(1)(iii)(A) would count it as an affiliate directly controlling its own subsidiaries (NOTES.md). The default is the first constructor of `Self-affiliation` and the value the tests call `default readings`; the caller supplies the choice.

witnesses: regw-independent-tests.l4 lines 1185-1188 (R1), fixture `f p30`: Bank is not an affiliate under the default readings and is one under `literal self readings`
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph on the member bank being its own affiliate on the literal words, and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 6; independent-readings.md R1.
A switch: the record `Readings` (regw-nouns.l4, lines 143-147) is an input of every function that answers the question, and both constructors execute.

source.quote: Any company in which a majority of its directors, trustees, or general partners (or individuals exercising similar functions) constitute a majority of the persons holding any such office with the member bank or any company that controls the member bank

readings.description: Constructor `One board at a time: the member bank, or one controlling company`. “any company that controls the member bank” is read as any one company: a company is an affiliate if a majority of its directors are a majority of the member bank's board, or of one controlling company's board.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(4): “Any company in which a majority of its directors, trustees, or general partners (or individuals exercising similar functions) constitute a majority of the persons holding any such office with the member bank or any company that controls the member bank”

readings.description: Constructor `The offices of the member bank and of every controlling company pooled`. The offices of the member bank and of every controlling company are pooled, and the question is whether a majority of the company's directors is a majority of the pool. Both readings count “a majority” as more than half of each group.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(4): “Any company in which a majority of its directors, trustees, or general partners (or individuals exercising similar functions) constitute a majority of the persons holding any such office with the member bank or any company that controls the member bank”

taken.rationale: decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review: “any company” is read as any one company (independent-readings.md R2). The two readings differ in both directions. The default is the first constructor of `Interlock reading` and the value the tests call `default readings`; the caller supplies the choice.

witnesses: regw-independent-tests.l4 lines 1205-1210 (R2): `f il pooled` (Co is not an affiliate one board at a time and is one when pooled) and `f il parent board` (Co is an affiliate one board at a time and is not when pooled)
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph on 223.2(a)(4) (a switch), and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 3; independent-readings.md R2.
A switch in the record `Readings`; both constructors execute.

source.quote: Directly controlled by: (A) One or more affiliates (other than depository institution affiliates) of the member bank; or (B) A shareholder that controls the member bank or a group of shareholders that together control the member bank

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(3): “A company controls securities, assets, or other ownership interests owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by any subsidiary”

readings.description: Constructor `Control through the controller's own holdings and elections, without attribution`. “Directly controlled” means control by the controller's own holdings, elections and Board determinations, without securities attributed from its subsidiaries under 223.3(g)(3).

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(b)(1)(iii): “Directly controlled by:”

readings.description: Constructor `Any control, including securities attributed from subsidiaries`. “Directly controlled” includes securities attributed from subsidiaries under 223.3(g)(3). With a parent P of the member bank and a subsidiary Sub of the bank, P controls Sub through the bank and Sub is an affiliate.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(3): “A company controls securities, assets, or other ownership interests owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by any subsidiary”

taken.rationale: decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review: 223.3(g) defines control and does not define “directly”, and the second reading would make the exclusion do almost no work for a subsidiary of a bank that has a corporate parent (NOTES.md). The default is the first constructor of `Direct control reading` and the value the tests call `default readings`; the caller supplies the choice.

witnesses: regw-independent-tests.l4 lines 1216-1220 (R3), fixture `f direct reading` (P controls the bank, the bank holds 60 percent of Sub, P holds nothing in Sub): Sub is not an affiliate under the default readings and is one under `any control readings`
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph headed 'directly controlled' in (b)(1)(iii)(A) and (B), and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 2; independent-readings.md R3.
The switch is read where the inquiry is built (regw-affiliate.l4, `inquiry about`, lines 28-31) and used by `is an excluded subsidiary` (line 246).
A switch in the record `Readings`; both constructors execute.

source.quote: (11) Subsidiaries of affiliates. Any subsidiary of a company described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (10) of this section

readings.description: Constructor `A subsidiary of a company described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (10) only`. The words as they stand: a company that is an affiliate only through (a)(11) or (a)(12) is not “described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (10)”, and a company the exclusions in (b) take out is still described.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(11): “(11) Subsidiaries of affiliates. Any subsidiary of a company described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (10) of this section”

readings.description: Constructor `A subsidiary of any affiliate, so that the prong chains`. The heading “Subsidiaries of affiliates”: a subsidiary of any affiliate found so far, after the exclusions. This replaces the literal reading and does not add to it.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(11): “Subsidiaries of affiliates”

taken.rationale: decided by Claude 2026-11-21, pending Meng's review: the default takes the words as they stand; the other takes the heading (NOTES.md). The two differ in both directions, and where the link is securities or directors the control test already carries it up, so they agree there. The default is the first constructor of `Prong 11 reading` and the value the tests call `default readings`; the caller supplies the choice.

witnesses: regw-independent-tests.l4 lines 1226-1229 (R4), fixture `f prong eleven premises`: Dd, a 30 percent company of an excluded premises company, is an affiliate under the default readings and is not under `chain readings`
regw-independent-tests.l4 lines 1240-1241 (R4), fixture `f subsidiary of a determined company`: DS is not an affiliate under the default readings and is one under `chain readings`
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph on (a)(11) “a company described in paragraphs (a)(1) through (10)” (a switch), and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 4; independent-readings.md R4.
The first rule defect of the independent test pass was in this switch: the chaining constructor had been a union, not the reading its name states (NOTES.md, ‘The independent test pass’, defect 1).
A switch in the record `Readings`; both constructors execute.

source.quote: (B) A shareholder that controls the member bank or a group of shareholders that together control the member bank

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(3): “shareholders who beneficially or otherwise control, directly or indirectly, by trust or otherwise, the member bank or any company that controls the member bank”

readings.description: (a)(3) says “shareholders who beneficially or otherwise control” and is read one shareholder at a time; a group of shareholders is not aggregated.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(3): “shareholders who beneficially or otherwise control, directly or indirectly, by trust or otherwise, the member bank or any company that controls the member bank”

readings.description: (a)(3) aggregates a group of shareholders that together control the member bank (or a company that controls it), as (b)(1)(iii)(B) says in terms for the exclusion.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(b)(1)(iii)(B): “(B) A shareholder that controls the member bank or a group of shareholders that together control the member bank”

taken.rationale: NOT MODELLED for groups. NOTES.md: whether (a)(3) aggregates a group is not stated, and the contrast with (b)(1)(iii)(B), which says so, can be read either way; the encoding takes one shareholder in both places and does not aggregate groups. The inputs carry one holder's holdings per row and no group of shareholders (independent-readings.md, ‘Not expressible with the inputs’).

notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘(a)(3) and (b)(1)(iii)(B): one shareholder at a time’, and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 5.

Second site: (b)(1)(iii)(B) is read through `directlyControlledByShareholder` in `is an excluded subsidiary` (regw-affiliate.l4, line 257). There the text names a group in terms and the encoding does not model it, which is a stated limit; the open reading question is (a)(3).
No test of the row aggregates a group: a search of its three test files for group, aggregate and “together control” found none, so the divergence is not assessed.

source.quote: no company will be deemed to control another company by virtue of its ownership or control of shares in a fiduciary capacity, except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of § 223.2 or if the company owning or controlling the shares is a business trust

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(1)(i): “The company or shareholder, directly or indirectly, or acting through one or more other persons, owns, controls, or has power to vote 25 percent or more of any class of voting securities of the other company”

readings.description: The bar is on a company: fiduciary shares held by an individual, or by a trust that is not a business trust (not a company under 223.3(f)), still count towards control.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(2): “no company will be deemed to control another company by virtue of its ownership or control of shares in a fiduciary capacity, except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of § 223.2 or if the company owning or controlling the shares is a business trust”

12 CFR 223.3(g)(1)(i): “The company or shareholder, directly or indirectly, or acting through one or more other persons, owns, controls, or has power to vote 25 percent or more of any class of voting securities of the other company”

readings.description: No holder's fiduciary shares count towards control, whether a company, an individual or a plain trust.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(2): “no company will be deemed to control another company by virtue of its ownership or control of shares in a fiduciary capacity, except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of § 223.2 or if the company owning or controlling the shares is a business trust”

readings.foreclosure: The words are “no company”; reaching an individual or a plain trust would need 'no person' (NOTES.md).

taken.rationale: The words as written (NOTES.md, ‘(g)(2) fiduciary shares’). An earlier version of the rules barred every holder; the independent test pass found it and it was changed (NOTES.md, ‘The independent test pass’, defect 3).

witnesses: regw-independent-tests.l4 lines 1300-1307 (R14), fixtures `f fiduciary plain trust` and `f fiduciary individual holder`: a plain trust or an individual holding 30 percent as fiduciary controls T on the taken reading and does not on the other
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘(g)(2) fiduciary shares’, and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 8; independent-readings.md R14.

The second reading is the one NOTES.md names (“the other reading, that no holder's fiduciary shares count, would need "no person"”) and independent-readings.md R14 (“the exclusion covers every holder”). The citation of 223.3(g)(1)(i) belongs to the taken reading: independent-readings.md R14 gives it as the reason an individual or a plain trust controls.

source.quote: The company or shareholder controls in any manner the election of a majority of the directors, trustees, or general partners (or individuals exercising similar functions) of the other company

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(3): “A company controls securities, assets, or other ownership interests owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by any subsidiary”

readings.description: An election link from a company's subsidiary, or from a subsidiary of that subsidiary, counts for the company, as 223.3(g)(3) counts the securities its subsidiaries hold. P controls S by 30 percent and S controls the election of T's directors: P controls T.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(1)(ii): “The company or shareholder controls in any manner the election of a majority of the directors, trustees, or general partners (or individuals exercising similar functions) of the other company”

readings.description: 223.3(g)(3) attributes “securities, assets, or other ownership interests” and not powers, so an election exercised through a subsidiary is not carried up: P does not control T.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(3): “A company controls securities, assets, or other ownership interests owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by any subsidiary”

taken.rationale: “in any manner” in (g)(1)(ii) (NOTES.md, ‘(g)(1)(ii) through a subsidiary’). An earlier version counted only an election link from the controller itself; the independent test pass found it and it was changed (NOTES.md, ‘The independent test pass’, defect 2). A Board determination under (g)(1)(iii) is about the pair it names and is not passed up.

witnesses: regw-independent-tests.l4 lines 1262-1267 (R7), fixture `f election through a subsidiary`: P controls T on the taken reading and does not on the other
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘(g)(1)(ii) through a subsidiary’, and ‘Open questions for a lawyer’ item 9; independent-readings.md R7.

source.quote: by or for the benefit of shareholders who beneficially or otherwise control, directly or indirectly, by trust or otherwise, the member bank or any company that controls the member bank

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(2): “except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of § 223.2”

readings.description: The exception “as provided in paragraph (a)(3)” is encoded for the limb that needs no beneficiary: a shareholder that controls the member bank and itself holds shares of Co as a fiduciary controls Co for 223.2(a)(3), reading the “by” limb of “by or for the benefit of shareholders” as the shareholder acting as trustee. Its control of the member bank itself is judged without them.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(3): “by or for the benefit of shareholders who beneficially or otherwise control, directly or indirectly, by trust or otherwise, the member bank or any company that controls the member bank”
12 CFR 223.3(g)(2): “except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of § 223.2”

readings.description: The limb “for the benefit of shareholders” also reaches shares that someone else holds as a fiduciary for the benefit of shareholders who control the member bank. This turns on who the beneficiaries are, and the inputs carry no beneficiary, so it is not encoded.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.2(a)(3): “by or for the benefit of shareholders who beneficially or otherwise control, directly or indirectly, by trust or otherwise, the member bank or any company that controls the member bank”

readings.description: The exception is only for shares held “for the benefit of” such shareholders by someone else, so the fiduciary holder's own control stays excluded and Co is not an affiliate where a company that controls the member bank is itself the trustee (independent-readings.md R16). An individual trustee is an affiliate on either reading while F8 stands.

citations.cite: 12 CFR 223.3(g)(2): “except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of § 223.2”

taken.rationale: NOT MODELLED for the “for the benefit of” limb. The code encodes the limb with the shareholder itself as trustee (the `fid` switch of `holding counts`, regw-control.l4, and `prong 3`), and not the limb that needs a beneficiary (NOTES.md, ‘(g)(2) fiduciary shares’).

witnesses: regw-independent-tests.l4 lines 1318-1327 (R16), fixture `f fiduciary corporate trustee` (a company TC holds 30 percent of the bank and 30 percent of Co as fiduciary): Co is an affiliate on the taken reading and is not on `benefitLimbOnly`
notes: Trace: NOTES.md, section ‘Forks and open questions’, the paragraph ‘(g)(2) fiduciary shares’, which says the limb for the benefit of shareholders is not encoded; independent-readings.md R16.

Only `f fiduciary corporate trustee` separates the readings: the individual in `f fiduciary individual` is outside the (g)(2) bar on the taken reading of F8, so Co is an affiliate there either way (independent-readings.md R16).
